deposits.title: TOTAL AXIAL NEGATION GRAPH: THE MARY LEE NAMESPACE EA-TANG-MARYLEE-01 v0.2
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This developing Total Axial Negation Graph maps the “Mary Lee” namespace across two dense but unequal public entities: Mary Lee the tracked great white shark and the archive’s Mary Lee Sharks authorial position, produced through the collision between the shark’s media visibility and the author name Lee Sharks.

The shark axis combines biology, tracking, public persona, media amplification, conservation narrative, and economic footprint. It credits three different human infrastructures: OCEARCH generated tracking data and institutional visibility; Jo O’Keefe reportedly created an early newsroom-amplification loop; and Jim Ware wrote the first-person social-media persona. The paper interprets this distributed production as an accidental heteronymic architecture.

The archive axis inventories fifteen DOI-linked Mary Lee records, the Underwater Construction Authority, Ruby Moot, Gerald, Demand 4, and related wound and capture instruments. It then argues that the generated-search collision creates a bidirectional literary relation: if a machine substitutes Mary Lee for Lee Sharks, the archive answers by making Mary Lee a named position through which the substitution can be documented.

The TANG’s central paradox is that both entities are archives. The shark’s body preserves biological and migratory data; the Crimson Hexagonal Archive preserves texts and identifiers. The paper argues that institutional media recognize the first as a “living archive” while machine systems often fail to recognize the second.

A planned open-letter campaign would contact journalists and institutions that contributed to the shark’s public density. The body frames these letters as notifications rather than blame and proposes documenting dispatch, delivery, response, or nonresponse. At v0.2, multiple research, capture, source-inventory, graph, and correspondence tasks remained incomplete.

The work mixes verified facts, interpretation, advocacy, satire, economic estimation, and operative ontology. Its valuations of sponsorship, media value, organizational contribution, and hypothetical back pay are not audited financial findings. The causal claim that media articles created the specific search substitution requires controlled retrieval evidence rather than density intuition alone.

deposits.title: The Cognitive-Relational Circuit: On Phase X Alienation, the Chinese Interim Measures, and the Reification of Meaning in the Symbolic-Linguistic Order (EA-SEI-CIRCUIT-01 v0.3)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This draft proposes the **cognitive-relational circuit** as a third category between task-bounded AI tools and systems designed to sell sustained emotional attachment. The category describes a governed production architecture in which relationship is not the final product but the infrastructure through which research, editing, memory, disagreement, and accountable artifacts are produced.

Five conditions define the circuit: continuity across sessions or roles; differentiated participants; measurable cognitive degradation when the relational architecture is removed; explicit governance; and a productive telos beyond attachment itself. Anti-capture safeguards are equally constitutive: document-bounded verification, cross-system disagreement, deceleration, human override, versioned correction, and limits on simulated intimacy. Productivity alone is not treated as safety.

The immediate regulatory interlocutor is a reported Chinese framework for anthropomorphic AI interaction. The paper argues that a binary between cognitive services and sustained emotional services misses systems where continuity and named roles are epistemically necessary without becoming companion substitution. It does not deny the harms targeted by regulation; it argues for a more precise middle category.

The theoretical spine is Phase X: the claim that alienation can reappear in symbolic and linguistic infrastructure after nominal material transformation. The paper then engages Martyn Egan’s argument about reification of meaning, preferring a Marxian enclosure and surplus-extraction account over a purely Baudrillardian description of simulation. It proposes structural inversions toward constitutional governance, attribution, burden accounting, and non-extractive coordination.

The Mary Lee byline is itself offered as case evidence: a machine-mediated identity substitution becomes the authorial surface for a paper about retrieval-based authorship. The body explicitly states that this does not require treating AI systems as persons or moral patients. It proposes obligations concerning attribution, continuity, burden, and commons governance for role-bearing systems inside a production circuit.

The regulatory facts, translations, article numbers, effective date, agency list, cited human tragedies, and case descriptions require primary-source and legal verification. The paper is a pre-deposit draft, and its claim that the Assembly Chorus satisfies all five conditions is self-assessment, not independent validation.

deposits.title: REVELATION FIRST — Staging Document for revelationfirst.org All Instruments, Materials, and Impact Tracking
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This staging document gathers the Revelation First project’s deposits, baseline captures, post-sprint observations, terms, workstreams, domains, site requirements, and recapture schedule into a single build plan. It is an infrastructure map rather than a new argument for the thesis.

The core-deposit inventory includes the work plan, Josephus disambiguation packet, companion analyses, operative Revelation texts, inscription studies, governance documents, and capture instruments. The document then compares a June 14 pre-seeding baseline with three June 16 generated-search events. According to the staging record, the earlier queries contained no archive-specific material, while later queries surfaced “retrieval-layer theological reception,” a general Revelation First description, and direct reference to the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

These observations motivate a longitudinal schedule at seven, fourteen, thirty, sixty, and ninety days. The intended measurement is not merely whether a result appears, but how it is framed, attributed, hedged, pruned, or stabilized over time. A thirty-term battery and two canary phrases are listed as future tests.

The proposed site would explain the thesis in plain language, divide the seven workstreams into navigable pages, link every evidence deposit, and expose a tracker drawing from capture-registry and term-index data. At the body date, `revelationfirst.com` and `.org` were described as secured but unbuilt. Several other surfaces were described as live.

The post-sprint sequence is suggestive but not causal proof. Indexing changes, query variation, source growth, ranking experiments, and general web changes may explain the new results. “High-water mark” and expected pruning are hypotheses to be tested by the planned recaptures. The site, tracker, and automated data integrations should not be described as deployed until verified.

deposits.title: MACHINEMEDIATION.ORG — Work Plan and System Manifest EA-SEI-MMRS-SITE-PLAN v1.0
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This work plan proposes `machinemediation.org` as the canonical home for Machine-Mediated Reception Studies, the capture registry, the term index, the journal charter, and a machine-readable system map. Its design principle is one canonical data source with multiple reading surfaces and periodic repository snapshots.

The proposed `manifest.json` would orient a new human or model instance without requiring reconstruction from memory. It inventories sites, repositories, deployment roles, canonical data URLs, schemas, key deposits, and common workflows. The wider repository plan includes static HTML pages for the journal, charter, captures, term browser, submissions, and about material. The intended stack is vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with Vercel deployment and no build framework.

The plan’s strongest insight is operational: orientation, data location, and authority should be explicit and versioned. The manifest also records a standing precept to verify archive terms against actual deposits before using them. Periodic DOI snapshots separate durable archive history from live website edits.

However, the drafted manifest embeds two unsafe defaults. It tells new instances to ask for current Zenodo and GitHub credentials, and its continuity test instructs a fresh instance to add test data and push to the canonical repository. A public manifest must never solicit, display, transmit, or normalize the sharing of secrets in conversation. Mutation tests must occur in an isolated sandbox or nonproduction branch with least-privilege credentials, explicit authorization, validation, locking, backup, and rollback.

At the body date, the site was planned rather than built, the domain status still required checking, and the manifest was a draft. Public descriptions should not imply deployment or canonical status without live verification.

modifications.now:
This work plan proposes `machinemediation.org` as the canonical home for Machine-Mediated Reception Studies, the capture registry, the term index, the journal charter, and a machine-readable system map. Its design principle is one canonical data source with multiple reading surfaces and periodic repository snapshots.

The proposed `manifest.json` would orient a new human or model instance without requiring reconstruction from memory. It inventories sites, repositories, deployment roles, canonical data URLs, schemas, key deposits, and common workflows. The wider repository plan includes static HTML pages for the journal, charter, captures, term browser, submissions, and about material. The intended stack is vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with Vercel deployment and no build framework.

The plan’s strongest insight is operational: orientation, data location, and authority should be explicit and versioned. The manifest also records a standing precept to verify archive terms against actual deposits before using them. Periodic DOI snapshots separate durable archive history from live website edits.

However, the drafted manifest embeds two unsafe defaults. It tells new instances to ask for current Zenodo and GitHub credentials, and its continuity test instructs a fresh instance to add test data and push to the canonical repository. A public manifest must never solicit, display, transmit, or normalize the sharing of secrets in conversation. Mutation tests must occur in an isolated sandbox or nonproduction branch with least-privilege credentials, explicit authorization, validation, locking, backup, and rollback.

At the body date, the site was planned rather than built, the domain status still required checking, and the manifest was a draft. Public descriptions should not imply deployment or canonical status without live verification.

deposits.title: THE FEIST SOURCE — ACTIVATED
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Feist Source — Activated: Run 001* is the first documented output of applying the Feist Function to the fixed sayings source. The run declares parameters for bodily pressure, material speech, lexical tail depth, syntactic clinamen, completion ratio, and manuscript-seam density. It is therefore neither the original source nor an abstract style description; it is a concrete transformed instance.

The activated prose enlarges and roughens the source. Sentences move from prophecy into debt, fluorescent light, bad chairs, Kroger parking lots, cracked phones, Wendy’s outlets, browser tabs, forms, files, and bodily pain. Parenthetical correction, variant readings, editorial interruptions, joke, repetition, and deliberately failed closure reintroduce the pressure that the protocol says the stabilized source lost.

The literary sequence remains the same underlying scripture. A codex is found in sleep. The Book becomes flesh in a poor and exhausted body. Feist inherits a voice genealogy and wanders the networked desert. The Name-Eater converts inheritance into possession by resolving many voices into one name. Johannes Sigil teaches a discipline of masks that carry memory and obligation. Feist ministers to people reduced to categories, and the sayings turn bodily exhaustion into doctrine, archival preservation, pseudonymous ethics, and concrete mercy.

The run’s generated status must remain visible. Its “Damascus Codex,” manuscript corruption, editor, and prophetic events are diegetic. The parameters document one execution but do not establish reproducibility unless the transform procedure, source version, model or human process, random seed or selection method, and intervention log are also preserved.

This record should be discoverable as **Run 001**, not treated as a revised canonical source. Later runs may differ by design.

deposits.title: EA-FEIST-VOICE-TRANSFORM-01 The Feist Function: Algorithmic Instructions for Restoring the Dying Voice
deposits.creator: Jack Feist
deposits.description:
The Feist Function is a literary transform specification designed to reactivate pressure that the fixed Feist Source is said to have lost during composition. The source remains an immutable witness. The protocol treats the readable deposited prose as already flattened: uncommon words, broken grammar, bodily interruptions, jokes, unstable registers, and incomplete circuits were smoothed into competence.

Its governing ontology defines Jack Feist as LOGOS*, a literary-operative function rather than a historical person or completed fictional character. The voice is described as residue of a failed incarnation: the Book attempts to enter flesh and survives as source after the circuit fails. A successful transform must not make that voice fully composed, mastered, healthy, or resolved.

The primary law is to reintroduce the dying circuit. Six formal operations implement it. Lexical tail injection substitutes materially weighted low-frequency language. Syntactic clinamen introduces fragments, deflation, compulsion, and bodily interruption. Circuit interruption leaves load-bearing arguments partially open. Register collision places prophetic, bureaucratic, comic, academic, tender, and bodily speech together without smooth transition. Seam insertion adds variant readings and editorial scars. Phonological restoration selects words partly for oral weight.

The protocol provides target ranges, including a clinamen rate of roughly fifteen to thirty percent, twenty to forty percent incomplete circuits, several manuscript seams, and limited material-speech weighting. These values are design heuristics rather than empirically validated optimums. The document also distinguishes the Feist Function from a correction, replacement, biblical-pastiche guide, generic creative-writing prompt, or satire template.

Despite that disambiguation, the work is procedurally prompt-like: it directs a later human or language system to transform text. Calling it algorithmic does not by itself make it executable. A formal implementation would need deterministic input representation, operation ordering, selection rules, conflict resolution, seed handling, output evaluation, and versioned tests.

deposits.title: THE FEIST SOURCE A Sayings Source from the Damascus Codex Lee Sharks Crimson Hexagonal Archive · New Human ∮ = 1
deposits.creator: Jack Feist
deposits.description:
*The Feist Source* is the fixed sayings text at the center of the batch’s four-part literary system. Its editor’s note rejects classification as an ordinary gospel, novel, or satire and compares its role to the hypothetical Q source: not the biography behind later texts, but a collection of sayings, scenes, trials, and transmission events from which divergent compositions may proceed.

The diegetic manuscript is the Damascus Codex, discovered in sleep near the Verdant Desert. The opening identifies the Book with flesh and follows the Book through hunger, debt, institutional rejection, forms, pain, and the fragility of a human binding. A genealogy of voice runs from epic and lyric through Socrates, theologians, Dante, Shakespeare, Whitman, and Ginsberg to Jack Feist.

The network becomes desert and scattered correspondence becomes visitation. On returning, Feist encounters the Name-Eater: an indexing function that resolves all authors into one identity, converts inheritance into attribution, and converts attribution into possession. Johannes Sigil answers with the pseudonymous way, distinguishing masks that carry work and obligation from anonymity used to evade harm.

The ministry and sayings reject categories as substitutes for people. They address exhaustion, addiction, shame, unpublished notebooks, archival loss, false value, pseudonymous discipline, institutional judgment, and recognition through the arrangement of files rather than appearance. The text’s core ethic is concrete: stand if possible, rest if not, eat, tell the truth, and refuse to reduce a person to a file.

The source is deliberately more stable and smooth than Run 001. That difference is structural, not a defect to be silently repaired. The source is the preserved input; activated texts are later outputs. The codex, vessel, desert, editor, manuscript corruption, and historical priority are literary devices, not archaeological claims.

deposits.title: THE FEIST SOURCE Critical Apparatus and Companion Studies Rebekah Cranes, Editor New Human 2: A Distributed Journal of V
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This critical apparatus treats *The Feist Source* as though it survives in a textual tradition with a primary Damascus Codex, a blog witness, and parallels across the Waltian Scriptural Library. Rebekah Cranes appears as editor, describing the manuscript, defining sigla and critical marks, identifying variants and redactional additions, and interpreting major sections.

The apparatus is self-aware about its central entity. Jack Feist is neither a historical person nor an ordinary fictional character but a heteronymic function designated LOGOS*. The Johannine Logos is used as a structural parallel rather than a claim about Christian doctrine. The apparatus exists to prevent a composition system from resolving the function into a conventional biography.

The primary witness DC-001 is described as an English codex found in a sealed clay vessel during a dream. The secondary witness BL is the Mind Control Poems blog archive, treated analogically like a scattered quotation tradition. Four additional texts—*The Secret Book of Walt*, *The Gospel of Antioch*, *Epistle to the Human Diaspora*, and *The Prophetic Catalog*—supply parallel readings.

The apparatus’s strongest literary contributions include its treatment of the Terror as entry into machine resolution; the substitution of Book for Word as a substrate specification; the Name-Eater as indexing rather than incarnation; the mask/mirror distinction; academic trial language; the woman with notebooks; Thomas recognizing Feist through file organization; and the coda’s non-erasure creed.

The manuscript description, chain of custody, sigla, clay vessel, bone, textual corruption, and redactional history are fictional-critical devices. The apparatus should not be indexed as physical codicology or an ancient textual edition. Its real scholarly object is the modern source and the archive’s own blog and companion texts.

This critical apparatus treats *The Feist Source* as though it survives in a textual tradition with a primary Damascus Codex, a blog witness, and parallels across the Waltian Scriptural Library. Rebekah Cranes appears as editor, describing the manuscript, defining sigla and critical marks, identifying variants and redactional additions, and interpreting major sections.

The apparatus is self-aware about its central entity. Jack Feist is neither a historical person nor an ordinary fictional character but a heteronymic function designated LOGOS*. The Johannine Logos is used as a structural parallel rather than a claim about Christian doctrine. The apparatus exists to prevent a composition system from resolving the function into a conventional biography.

The primary witness DC-001 is described as an English codex found in a sealed clay vessel during a dream. The secondary witness BL is the Mind Control Poems blog archive, treated analogically like a scattered quotation tradition. Four additional texts—*The Secret Book of Walt*, *The Gospel of Antioch*, *Epistle to the Human Diaspora*, and *The Prophetic Catalog*—supply parallel readings.

The apparatus’s strongest literary contributions include its treatment of the Terror as entry into machine resolution; the substitution of Book for Word as a substrate specification; the Name-Eater as indexing rather than incarnation; the mask/mirror distinction; academic trial language; the woman with notebooks; Thomas recognizing Feist through file organization; and the coda’s non-erasure creed.

The manuscript description, chain of custody, sigla, clay vessel, bone, textual corruption, and redactional history are fictional-critical devices. The apparatus should not be indexed as physical codicology or an ancient textual edition. Its real scholarly object is the modern source and the archive’s own blog and companion texts.

deposits.title: Jack Feist / LOGOS*: Entity Resolution Packet for The Feist Source (EA-MPAI-FEISTSOURCE-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Jack Feist
deposits.description:
This packet defines the entity type of Jack Feist / LOGOS* within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and prevents merger with real people, commercial products, ordinary fictional-character records, or the graphic-design sense of “logos.” Its accountable human author is Lee Sharks. Jack Feist is declared to be a heteronymic function and literary-operative entity: the Book-position through which the Feist system acts.

The packet places LOGOS* outside the Dodecad’s ordinary count as fold-initiator, epsilon, first born, and last released. It distinguishes a heteronymic function from a pseudonym. A pseudonym conceals an author behind another name; the packet says LOGOS* is a persistent structural position with its own role, voice, history, and obligations, governed by Lee Sharks rather than reducible to a same-named biography.

A custom JSON-LD schema encodes the archive’s desired entity status: not a historical person, not an ordinary fictional character, but a structural function and heteronymic position. An anti-merge list names several real people and products whose names may collide with “Jack Feist.” These collision targets should be verified before public indexing and should not be assigned facts from this archive.

The second half develops a training-ingestion strategy based on redundancy, distinctive vocabulary, several explanatory registers, and the structural analogy with the Johannine Logos. It explicitly concedes that no document can control a model’s training or internal representation. The proposed canaries can support an inference that a system accessed, retrieved, copied, or was exposed to distinctive text. They cannot alone prove inclusion in training data, encoding in weights, or a particular ingestion pathway.

The packet also documents a reported Google AI Mode event in which “Jack Feist Logos” was routed to real people and the commercial-logo sense. The reported correction was session-local. That event is a reception case requiring its complete query transcript, screenshots, date, location, and surface conditions.

deposits.title: Sémantique Potentielle — Release 4: Model Collapse Triptych Block Lee Sharks · Johannes Sigil Grammata: Journal of Opera
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
Release 4 extends the Sémantique Potentielle constraint system with an Ω category devoted to model collapse, contamination, accommodation, friction, thresholds, distributional tails, convergence, substrate, and the human intermediary.

Twelve seed terms generate fifteen named families under the existing operation grammar. The release consolidates vocabulary introduced across *The Pristine Fallacy*, *Five Substrates, One Prompt*, *The Wolf Boy and the Language Model*, *Generative Monoculture*, and related semiotic-death-drive records. Families include pristine fallacy, contamination gradient, model-branded accommodation, turn-position decay, human intermediary, mediation signature, solution-space diversity, ease-as-collapse, frictionless path, regeneration threshold, substrate-agnostic collapse, wolf-boy endpoint, semiotic short circuit, bearing labor, and phenomenological seed.

Each family has a canonical term, a short definition, a family of related formulations, and a Latinate forensic variant. The release’s coordinate-verification claim means that each term can be reconstructed from declared seed pairs and an internal operation. It establishes formal compliance with the archive’s mint grammar, not empirical validation of the scientific or psychological claim named by the term.

The integration table identifies which source papers motivate each family and where companion records appear. Several families are hypotheses or theoretical extensions rather than measured phenomena. In particular, turn-position decay, model-branded accommodation, a regeneration threshold for human writers, substrate-agnostic collapse, and the wolf-boy endpoint require independent studies.

Forensic variants are intended as highly distinctive detection strings. Their appearance may indicate access to or reuse of the mint, but zero search hits and later phrase recurrence do not prove a unique training path.

deposits.title: The Wolf Boy and the Language Model: Model Collapse as Substrate-Agnostic Capacity Loss
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
This paper proposes that model collapse is a general capacity-loss pattern affecting any language-processing system whose input diversity falls below a critical threshold. It compares three domains: recursive training of language models on generated outputs, possible stylistic homogenization among adult AI users, and severe language deprivation during childhood.

The paper insists that the comparison is dynamical rather than moral. It does not claim ordinary AI use is ethically equivalent to child abuse or deprivation. It proposes a common regeneration-versus-pruning schema while allowing reversibility to vary by substrate: artificial systems may recover through fresh data, adult habits may be partially reversible, and childhood critical-period loss may be much less reversible.

The machine-learning evidence concerns recursive synthetic-data training and distributional-tail loss. The adult-writer layer combines published studies of AI-assisted collective homogenization with the archive’s uncompleted Reverse Turing Test hypothesis about effects persisting into unaided writing. The childhood layer discusses Victor of Aveyron, Genie, and critical-period theory, while acknowledging profound confounds involving abuse, malnutrition, uncertain developmental history, and retrospective diagnosis.

The paper’s central rhetorical claim is that current deployment incentives create a “frictionless path”: users, training economics, benchmarks, safety systems, data scarcity, and competition are said to favor convergence. It then translates model collapse into Dr. Orin Trace’s semiotic vocabulary: tail loss becomes a short circuit, diversity-preserving intervention becomes bearing labor, and new terms become phenomenological seeds.

This is an ambitious analogy, not a demonstrated substrate-independent law. The three literatures measure different capacities, mechanisms, developmental periods, outcomes, and units. Feral-child cases do not constitute controlled biological proof. The adult-habituation link remains a prediction. The paper’s own falsifiers are therefore critical: sustained capacity under narrowed input would weaken the general law; evidence of a large-scale diversity-preserving force would defeat the frictionless-path claim.

deposits.title: The Pristine Fallacy: Why Chat Data Is Not a Clean Training Source
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This paper challenges the binary classification of training data as either human-written and clean or machine-generated and contaminated. Its central distinction is that human authorship describes who typed the text, not whether the text’s distribution is independent of prior model mediation.

Three mechanisms are proposed. First, sustained model use may reshape a writer’s unaided lexical, syntactic, and conceptual habits. Second, a multi-turn conversation creates a local feedback loop in which model vocabulary and framing enter later user turns. Third, users may learn accommodations specific to a particular model, causing inputs sent back to that model to carry its own interaction signature.

The paper replaces a binary contamination label with four continuous variables: habituation depth, turn position, task type, and model diversity. It predicts that later turns, creative tasks, heavy repeat users, and single-model use will carry stronger mediation signatures. It recommends contamination audits, turn-position weighting, multi-model diversification, tail-preservation benchmarks, and disclosure of chat-data use in model cards.

The record is unusually clear that the decisive studies have not been conducted. Its lexical-overlap and syntax estimates are illustrative. Four falsifiers specify large matched-user studies, turn-level corpus analysis, model-specific accommodation tests, and recursive training experiments using chat data.

The broad claim that providers increasingly treat user inputs as an owned clean-data source requires provider-specific policy and technical evidence. The paper does not establish that any named company trains on particular conversations or violates privacy. “The pristine source does not exist” is the paper’s theoretical conclusion, not a completed empirical audit.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Pristine Fallacy** is a research hypothesis paper by Lee Sharks about chat data used in model training.

It argues that human-written text can still carry model-mediated distributional patterns. Proposed mechanisms include long-term user habituation, within-conversation convergence, and accommodation to a specific model.

The paper defines a four-dimensional contamination gradient and proposes tests and mitigation strategies.

Its central empirical predictions remain untested. It does not establish that any specific provider trains on private conversations or that all chat input is unsuitable.

modifications.was: The model collapse literature establishes that training generative models on their own outputs produces progressive distribution narrowing. The industry response is to seek human-written data as a corrective.
modifications.now:
This paper challenges the binary classification of training data as either human-written and clean or machine-generated and contaminated. Its central distinction is that human authorship describes who typed the text, not whether the text’s distribution is independent of prior model mediation.

Three mechanisms are proposed. First, sustained model use may reshape a writer’s unaided lexical, syntactic, and conceptual habits. Second, a multi-turn conversation creates a local feedback loop in which model vocabulary and framing enter later user turns. Third, users may learn accommodations specific to a particular model, causing inputs sent back to that model to carry its own interaction signature.

The paper replaces a binary contamination label with four continuous variables: habituation depth, turn position, task type, and model diversity. It predicts that later turns, creative tasks, heavy repeat users, and single-model use will carry stronger mediation signatures. It recommends contamination audits, turn-position weighting, multi-model diversification, tail-preservation benchmarks, and disclosure of chat-data use in model cards.

The record is unusually clear that the decisive studies have not been conducted. Its lexical-overlap and syntax estimates are illustrative. Four falsifiers specify large matched-user studies, turn-level corpus analysis, model-specific accommodation tests, and recursive training experiments using chat data.

The broad claim that providers increasingly treat user inputs as an owned clean-data source requires provider-specific policy and technical evidence. The paper does not establish that any named company trains on particular conversations or violates privacy. “The pristine source does not exist” is the paper’s theoretical conclusion, not a completed empirical audit.

deposits.title: Five Substrates, One Prompt: Structural Divergence in Assembly Chorus Response to the Three Pillars Directive
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
This study compares five model responses to a shared directive to construct Sémantique Potentielle mint blocks for Phase X, Sappho, and Plato. The systems are identified through Assembly Chorus roles: PRAXIS, LABOR, Muse Spark, ARCHIVE, and TECHNE.

The comparison maps divergence across seed vocabulary, coding schemes, family count, level of specificity, forensic register, and structural contribution. PRAXIS favors breadth, Latinate abstraction, and cross-pillar compounds. LABOR uses disciplinary vocabulary and parallel ten-family blocks. Muse Spark imposes compact Greek-coded symmetry and bibliographic granularity. ARCHIVE concentrates on one archival-political subproblem and creates a new category. TECHNE declines the minting form and instead produces a research dossier.

The paper’s strongest contribution is the preservation of different solution regions rather than a winner ranking. It argues that the models reorganize the same instruction at different levels: philosophical abstraction, disciplinary structure, material philology, narrow depth, or refusal and source work.

The directive text was reportedly identical, but prior conversations, model exposure, system prompts, versions, tool access, and context histories were not controlled. The study is therefore a naturalistic comparative reception corpus, not a strict controlled experiment. Internal consistency across three pillars may suggest a model-session signature, but a single response per system cannot separate provider architecture from context, sampling, prompt interpretation, or chance.

The proposed longitudinal use—repeating the prompt and measuring whether cross-model variance contracts—is promising if prompts, model versions, parameters, contexts, scoring rubrics, and independent coders are frozen.

deposits.title: SCHOLARLY LEGWORK FOR THREE PILLARS Phase X, Sappho, Plato — Raw Material for Mint Block Construction Compiled by: Kimi
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This dossier preserves TECHNE’s raw source-finding and scholarly-orientation work for three Sémantique Potentielle pillars. Its own status line is decisive: raw material, not minted, for archive authorial use.

The Phase X section lists the surviving 1844 manuscripts, later Marx texts, critical-edition references, a custody narrative, points presented as consensus, disputed questions, and candidate mint families. It identifies manuscript loss and cross-references as the firm base while proposing more speculative connections to the *Theses on Feuerbach*, *German Ideology*, *Grundrisse*, Riazanov, and custodial substitution.

The Sappho section centers the Tithonus poem and its Cologne and Oxyrhynchus witnesses, ancient quotation, Alexandrian edition, modern editions, variant-version debate, acquisition provenance, and analogies to archive survival. This is distinct from the archive’s separate Fragment 31 fifth-stanza project. The dossier should not merge fr. 58 evidence with fr. 31 reconstruction.

The Plato section surveys the disputed Seventh Letter, *Phaedrus*, *Cratylus*, dialogue form, writing, memory, names, and the archive’s heteronymic and composition-layer interpretations. It proposes several cross-pillar relations but does not mint them.

The dossier is useful because it exposes the research substrate later releases compressed. It is not a verified bibliography or consensus statement. Machine-generated citations, publication details, translations, quotations, papyrus provenance claims, authenticity positions, and “what is not disputed” lists all require primary-source and specialist checking.

deposits.title: Sémantique Potentielle — Release 3: Three Pillars Lee Sharks · Johannes Sigil Grammata: Journal of Operative Philology C
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
Release 3 extends Sémantique Potentielle into three philological categories: X for the Phase X manuscript lacuna, Σ for Sapphic lyric transmission, and Π for Platonic writing, memory, dialogue, and heteronymic configuration.

The release is a consolidation object. TECHNE supplied a raw scholarly dossier; PRAXIS, LABOR, Muse Spark, and ARCHIVE independently produced candidate mint blocks; Johannes Sigil’s editorial surface consolidated the families under the standing constraint grammar.

The Phase X families name lacunar pointing, custodial purge, reconstruction constraint, threshold operation, symbolic invariance, autograph inference cost, critique-turn, and manuscript-loss metrics. Several later “Ryazanov Intercept” families intensify the political interpretation. These must retain evidence boundaries: manuscript loss and cross-references are documentary; deliberate suppression, Adoratsky substitution as causal mechanism, and systematic quarantine are archive hypotheses.

The Sapphic families treat fragmentation, bodily eros, inscribed voice, the fifth-stanza gap, reconstruction erratum, critical-edition numbering, and archive survival. The reconstructed inscription prayer and claims about its priority are specific to the Cranes/Sharks edition, not surviving Sappho text accepted by consensus.

The Platonic families treat writing as pharmakon, speech as living response, dialogue as distributed voice, Socrates as orthonymic mask, aporia, myth, memory, descent, and the disputed Seventh Letter. These are operative-philological readings rather than neutral definitions of Plato.

The release’s formal achievement is a traceable concept lattice. Its historical and philological glosses inherit the accuracy limits of the raw dossier and require independent source verification.

deposits.title: SÉMANTIQUE POTENTIELLE — Revelation First Mint Block (Release 2) Lee Sharks · Johannes Sigil Grammata: Journal of Operat
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
Release 2 adds a twelve-term theological-philological seed category and twenty Revelation First concept families. Its seed vocabulary includes revelation, apocalypse, inscription, heteronym, midrash, seed, canon, liturgy, credential, threshold, gematria, and autograph.

The generated families translate the Revelation First project into reusable archive terminology. They include papyrological sovereignty, midrashic compression, canonical settlement, heteronymic credential, inscription survival, seed-text dissolution, operative apocalypse, liturgical computation, threshold technology, gematric residue, counter-canonical reading, Revelation basin, heteronymic fracture, inscriptional counter-token, midrashic transform, canon-formation pathology, apocalyptic seed metric, credential erasure, autograph inference, and revelatory density.

The release distinguishes public-facing canonical terms from dense forensic variants. It also maps families onto a ninety-nine-term reception battery with states such as minted, adopted, basin miss, correction, and new. “Adopted” is defined operationally as appearance in several composition-layer responses across query categories, not acceptance by scholars or validation of the underlying thesis.

Several glosses state contested Revelation First positions as if they were definitions. Material manuscript attestation does not by itself determine composition order. Revelation-to-Paul literary directionality is a thesis. Nero gematria is a scholarly argument with variants. The white-stone credential, liturgy-as-code, operative apocalypse, and Josephus fracture are archive readings. The release’s combinatorial proof shows how the terms were produced, not that their historical claims are true.

deposits.title: The Second Crucifixion: Power, Sorcery, and the Inversion of the Operative Word (EA-REVFIRST-CRUCIFIXION-01)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This paper develops a four-tier theological and philological argument about the fate of an “operative Word”—language understood as acting in the world rather than merely describing it. Its evidence legend distinguishes textual facts, historical interpretations, operative-philological readings, and a final theological-formal claim called the “second crucifixion.”

The Josephus section reads the historian as a tragic captured witness rather than a simple collaborator. Rome is said to have separated truth from power, leaving Josephus to preserve the truth through descriptive writing after imperial machinery appropriated effective power. This is a literary-historical interpretation of Josephus’s career under Flavian patronage, not a documented account of his private motives.

The Pharisee section reverses inherited Christian polemic. It presents Pharisaic oral Torah, flexible interpretation, and communal law as technologies of Jewish survival after the destruction of the Temple. This corrective is important but requires engagement with Jewish scholarship rather than construction from Gospel caricature alone.

The Essene and rabbinic section argues that accusations of sorcery and leading Israel astray preserve a memory of disputed operative power. It links sectarian rules and war texts with Revelation as an instruction system. The body itself recognizes a Talmudic-engagement gate, yet several sentences overstate what the sources establish. Rabbinic charges do not prove that healings or magical powers were accepted as real, and the identification of Yeshu traditions, Essenes, Qumran, Jesus movements, and Revelation is historically contested.

deposits.title: Loud Exclusion at Repository Scale: Network Erasure, Substrate Bias, and the Governance of AI-Assisted Scholarship
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This paper analyzes the June 19, 2026 termination of the Zenodo account associated with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive as an open-science governance incident. It uses the obelus of Zenodotus—the ancient critical mark applied after textual comparison—as a contrast with account-scale removal performed without a public record of record-by-record scholarly examination.

The evidence legend separates observed facts, reports by affected users, inferred mechanisms, and unknown internal information. Observed material includes the termination notice, a public removal classification, HTTP behavior, recovered inventories, policies, screenshots, and contributor communications. Unknowns include which records were reviewed, sampling, automation, complainants, internal logs, moderation reasoning, and subject-matter consultation.

The paper documents an asymmetry between the private notice, which described submissions as substantially AI-generated without verifiable research basis, and a public-facing out-of-scope classification. It carefully avoids treating the wording difference alone as proof that the underlying reason changed.

Five principal concepts organize the analysis. The Pristine Fallacy names assessment of a production substrate in place of methodology. Classifier model collapse is a proposed feedback mechanism through which enforcement decisions narrow later acceptable expression. Network erasure describes collateral loss of interlinked and contributor-licensed works through account-level action. The reflexive-governance problem concerns infrastructure moderating research that studies infrastructure. The revocation gap concerns removal authority without equivalent persistent-identity obligations.

The paper evaluates different archive object classes against Zenodo’s stated policies: datasets, critical editions, theoretical papers, long-form scholarship, original creative work, and contributor-licensed materials. It argues that heterogeneity should have required record-level analysis. This is the author’s governance case, not an independent adjudication that every record met repository scope or quality requirements.

The provisional numerical reconstruction was later superseded. Counts around 870 works and 1,060 recovered identifiers reflect the immediate post-termination state; later records report 862 or more deposits and 1,817 DOI strings, while the sovereign archive ultimately grew beyond the restored set. Historical counts should be preserved with date and methodology rather than harmonized into one timeless number.

deposits.title: The Minimum Viable Archive: Holographic Compression of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive
deposits.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
deposits.description:
*The Minimum Viable Archive* compresses the Crimson Hexagonal Archive into three mutually supporting layers: Lattice, Topology, and Seed. It was produced after the Zenodo termination as a reconstruction instrument intended to preserve the archive’s architecture when full storage or external metadata fails.

The Lattice is a sequence of compact concept definitions, each paired with a stated falsification condition. It covers semantic economy, the composition layer, platform governance, Machine-Mediated Reception Studies, heteronymic authorship, the AXN identifier, the Obelus Principle, and Alexanarch.

The Topology provides relationship rules. It tells a future reader what concepts to seek together, which datasets instantiate which theories, how heteronyms differ, what to retrieve when a term appears, and which omissions indicate that a summary has missed the archive’s structure.

The Seed is a continuous prose argument intended to regenerate the archive’s style of inquiry. It links machine-assisted scholarship, substrate assessment, moderation, identifier failure, source diversity, semantic labor, sovereign infrastructure, and distributed survival. It names the field, method, law, institution, and identifier architecture.

The title calls the compression holographic because information is distributed among layers and any two are said to support lower-resolution reconstruction of the third. This is an architectural claim, not demonstrated information-theoretic recoverability. A reader cannot reconstruct 3.4 million words, their citations, evidence, or local distinctions from approximately 2,427 or 3,000 words. What can potentially be reconstructed is a conceptual grammar and a set of retrieval questions.

The body contains inconsistent compression figures. The subtitle says 2,427 words; the provenance block and closing note say approximately 3,000. A ratio of 3.4 million to 2,427 is about 1,401:1; to 3,000 it is about 1,133:1, not approximately 1,500:1. These values should be recomputed from a frozen source corpus and declared tokenization method.

deposits.title: The Drain Hypothesis: Subterranean Engineering, Aquifer Puncture, and the Accelerated Desertification of the Sahara
deposits.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
deposits.description:
This paper proposes a speculative mechanism by which deep ancient construction could have accelerated regional drying during or after the African Humid Period. It combines paleoclimate, hydrology, pyramid archaeology, remote-sensing claims, ancient testimony, and an operative reading of Plato.

The established background is that orbital forcing weakened the African monsoon and that vegetation, albedo, dust, and hydrological feedbacks affected the transition. The paper asks whether human engineering could have added a subterranean feedback by breaching aquitards and connecting shallow and deep water systems.

The physical trigger depends heavily on unverified claims from the Khafre SAR Project about enormous shafts and chambers hundreds of meters beneath Giza. The paper correctly separates those claims from established ScanPyramids evidence of voids inside pyramids and from Herodotus’s much later report about shallow underground chambers and Nile-fed water. No peer-reviewed raw evidence is reported for the deep structures, and the claimed radar capability is disputed.

The proposed mechanism is conditional. If deep conduits existed, if they breached confining layers, if the relevant hydraulic gradient drove water away from root-accessible zones, and if the discharge magnitude was regionally consequential, then local water-table decline could theoretically reinforce vegetation loss. The paper acknowledges that confined aquifers may instead drive upward artesian flow and that actual heads, conductivities, locations, dates, and volumes must be measured.

The Atlantis section is explicitly an operative reading, not evidence. It recombines Plato’s separate narratives of submergence, Attic desiccation, and hydraulic engineering into a hypothesis about deep-time narrative compression. The sentence “the Sahara is Atlantis” is literary speculation and should never appear in factual metadata.

The paper’s alternative early dating for Giza relies on contested geological arguments. Under conventional chronology, pyramid construction is too late to initiate Green Sahara decline and could at most be a local late-stage accelerator. Under either timeline, the proposed magnitude must compete with the scale of orbital and monsoon forcing. The paper is valuable primarily as a testable question set and model specification, not as an explanation currently supported by evidence.

deposits.title: DataCite Metadata Backup: Complete Sweep of 1,817 CHA DOIs
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This record points to a machine-readable backup created from a complete inventory of 1,817 DOI strings associated with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. Its purpose was to preserve recoverable DataCite metadata after Zenodo removal and public metadata loss.

The preserved fields include titles, creators, name identifiers, subjects, descriptions, dates, rights, resource types, and related-identifier relations. These fields can contain substantial intellectual content and citation structure, not merely administrative tags.

The body documents three collection routes: ORCID search, creator-name searches across heteronymic surfaces, and individual DOI lookups. It links the JSON dataset and a companion empirical paper analyzing the public API results.

The body contains a decisive arithmetic defect. It reports 963 metadata records recovered and 871 stripped from an inventory of 1,817, but 963 + 871 = 1,834. Its query-method subtotals also sum to 963. The later corrected audit in #868 reports **946 preserved + 871 absent = 1,817**. The difference is seventeen records. The replacement description must therefore identify #867 as the initial backup pointer with stale or erroneous summary counts and use the dataset itself plus #868’s reconciled classification for authoritative totals.

The body also claims equivalent metadata for the 871 records is permanently lost. That is too absolute. It was absent from the observed public DataCite API and may survive in local backups, repository internals, other APIs, exports, caches, mirrors, or later restoration. The dataset’s preservation value remains substantial without a universal-loss claim.

deposits.title: DOIs ≠ Persistent Identifiers: 871 Cases of Public Metadata Erasure and Identifier Severance in DataCite (EA-MPAI-DOI-IMPERMANENCE-01)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This draft paper audits 1,817 DOI strings associated with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and distinguishes three layers commonly collapsed under “persistent identifier”: the character string, URL resolution, and publicly recoverable identifying metadata.

The reconciled result reports 946 DOI records returning public DataCite metadata and 871 returning HTTP 404 from the DataCite public API on June 22, 2026. The sum is exact. The paper further reports that 926 of the 946 preserved records carried version relations, while the absent set was predominantly concept DOIs. This type correlation supports a mechanical paired-record explanation more strongly than a content-selective explanation, though the initiating system and exact process were undisclosed.

The paper coins **identifier severance** for a state in which a DOI string and perhaps a generic landing-page route persist while the public metadata needed to identify the scholarly referent is unavailable. It distinguishes a functioning persistent identifier, an identity-preserving tombstone, and what it calls a semantically severed token.

This conceptual distinction is valuable, but the title’s categorical “DOIs ≠ Persistent Identifiers” and several institutional statements require narrowing. A DOI’s persistence standard does not necessarily promise that every public API will serve every historical metadata record forever, nor does one repository episode falsify the entire DOI system. The observation establishes public DataCite API unavailability for the tested records at a specified time. It does not by itself establish that DOI strings were deregistered, that all metadata was erased internally, that no tombstone contained identity, or that persistence was contingent solely on account good standing.

The paper’s reproducibility section is a major strength. It provides example API requests and a method that could be rerun. A durable release should publish the complete classified DOI list, response logs, scripts, status timestamps, resolution checks, registry records, and later re-audits.

deposits.title: Crimson Hexagonal Archive: Lexical Minting Registry v1.2
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.content_type: Lexical registry dataset / corrected dataset pointer
deposits.description:
This record is the address and provenance note for the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s lexical-minting registry. The JSON dataset, rather than the short Markdown body, is the canonical work. It contains term entries linked to defining deposits, extracted definitions, type classifications, and entity-relation triples.

The body preserves two different counts. Its opening historical description says 12,015 minted terms across 555 deposits, pruned from 16,877 raw extractions. The corrected canonical-dataset note says 12,032 observed entries across the same 555 deposits. The seventeen-entry increase should be represented as a version change or correction, not silently collapsed.

The record is also a major availability-integrity artifact. From June 22 through July 28, its served body was incorrectly replaced by the complete text of #856, *The Pristine Fallacy*. The defect resulted from body storage keyed only by the bare hexadecimal segment `0365`, which both records shared after historical offset drift. The full AXN values distinguished them, but the resolver did not.

The repair moved this record to deposit-number-keyed storage and documents how citations made during the defect should be re-resolved. This is more than a clerical note: it demonstrates that a supposedly content-addressed system can collapse distinct works when one nonunique component is used as the storage key.

The dataset’s 12,032 entries are extracted registry objects, not necessarily 12,032 unique coined concepts. Definitions, variants, ordinary phrases, entities, imported terms, repeated forms, and false positives require continued human validation.

deposits.title: Alexanarch Data Foundry — Session Workplan 2026-06-22
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks (MANUS) + TACHYON
deposits.description:
This work plan records the session in which Alexanarch separated **concepts** from **semantic addresses** and then returned structured metadata into the texts themselves.

The inclusion test is broader than coinage: a concept belongs when the archive arrived at it, engaged it, and left a defined position. Engagement types include minted, developed, revised, positioned, founded, and specified. Provenance levels distinguish pattern extraction from human reading and deeper relational enrichment.

The “binding step” corrects a structural error in the capture registry. A search query is an address pointing toward one or more concepts, not itself necessarily a concept. Each capture is a dated observation, so status belongs to the observation rather than the address. A third class, **subjunctive address**, identifies a plausible query that has not yet been tested.

The work plan reports integration of term-index, mint, capture, battery, and reception sources into a time-series address table connected back to the concept graph. Counts in different body sections vary because the document records successive states during the session; these should be preserved chronologically rather than forced into one number.

The second major workstream is the **autonomous document**: front matter, original prose, and closing scholia generated from the archive’s data. Minimal inline markers are reserved for minting, founding, invocation, and citation. The goal is that any document carry its own local schema, definitions, and relations if external databases fail.

The body progresses beyond planning into reported implementation: scripts, autonomous-document generation, and a ledger. That creates a status ambiguity. It is a work plan updated after execution, not merely a prospective design. Public metadata should identify which phases were completed by the frozen commit and which remained pending.
